record.what_it_does: Cloud phone/contact-center system for business calls, SMS and AI voice agents.
record.auth_notes: OAuth (for Technology Partners building apps for many Aircall customers) gives a non-expiring Bearer token. Basic Auth uses api_id and api_token created in the company's Settings > API Keys, and only covers one's own account.
record.access_notes: Basic Auth API keys are self-serve for any Aircall customer, but this needs a paid Aircall account. I did not find a free tier or a free developer account. OAuth for multi-tenant use needs Technology Partner approval. The docs say it is "a requirement to be listed on the Aircall App Marketplace".
record.api_breadth_notes: REST at api.aircall.io/v1. Resources: users, teams, calls, conversations, contacts, tags, numbers, messages, campaigns, conversation intelligence, integrations, AI voice agents, analytics and webhooks.
record.mcp_notes: The Aircall developer FAQ (developer.aircall.io/docs/mcp-faqs) says "we don't offer an MCP server but stay tuned". The page is undated. Community and third-party servers exist: Allo, itaygadot111, StackOne, Zapier, Composio. Aircall also has a "Register a Public MCP" program for partners, so that its own AI agents can connect to partner MCP servers.
record.blocker_notes: A multi-user OAuth flow needs Aircall Technology Partner approval. Without it, each end user would have to paste their own api_id and api_token, which works but is clunky. Basic auth needs a paying Aircall customer account.

evidence.quote: It is a requirement to be listed on the Aircall App Marketplace.
The `api_id` is the _username_ and the `api_token` is the _password_
We can call back any endpoint of your choice, each time an event occurs on an Aircall account.
As of this writting we don't offer an MCP servier but stay tuned.

record.needs_human: Check whether Aircall now has an official MCP server, since the FAQ is undated and a newer blog hints at MCP. Also check whether an OpenAPI spec or a sandbox exists, and what the Technology Partner approval process involves. I did not read the whole API reference page.
